Tuned vs OTT Navigator

November 19, 2026

OTT Navigator, from Scillarium Studio, is a deep, highly configurable player that runs on phones, tablets and TV boxes. Tuned aims for fewer settings to learn and a player that gets out of your way. Here is how they compare.

At a glance

OTT NavigatorTuned
Where it runsAndroid phones, tablets, TVs and TV boxesAndroid phones, tablets, Chromebooks, Android TV and Google TV
Playlist typesProvider playlists (types not listed on the pages we read)Xtream Codes, M3U link or file, MAC portal, Plex, Jellyfin and Emby
TV guideSeveral guide sources, including your own; several guide layoutsXMLTV guide as a list or a full grid, with reminders
Catch-upYes, with filtersYes, on Xtream servers that keep recordings
RecordingNot stated by the developerYes, live and from the guide (Premium)
Pause and rewind live TVYes, when the provider keeps an archiveYes, up to an hour kept on the device (Premium)
Several channels at onceYes, a multi-window "studio" modeNo, on purpose: one stream connection at a time
Casting to a TVChromecastChromecast and DLNA, phone as remote
Picture-in-pictureYesYes
Offline downloadsNot stated by the developerFilms and episodes, whole seasons too (more than 3 at a time is Premium)
Profiles and parental controlsUser profilesUp to 6 profiles, kids profiles and PINs (Premium); adult categories locked behind a PIN
TraktNot stated by the developerTrakt and Simkl; Trakt can import watched history (Premium)
Film and show detailsNot stated by the developerTMDB ratings, trailers, cast and actor pages, saved on the device
SubtitlesNot stated by the developerFull caption styling, timing fix, and subtitle search for films and episodes
AdsNot stated by the developerNone, ever
PriceFree, with some advanced features paid (no price stated)Free; Premium US$9.99 a year with a 7-day trial, or US$24.99 once

"Not stated by the developer" means we couldn't find it on the developer's own pages or store listing. It may still be there, so check before you rule it out.

Price

OTT Navigator's core features are free and some advanced ones are paid; we couldn't find a price on the pages we read. Tuned is free, with Premium at US$9.99 a year with a 7-day trial or US$24.99 once.

Tuned's prices are what Google Play charges in the United States; Play shows them in your own currency. Premium covers up to three devices, and a Tuned account can add more.

Where OTT Navigator is ahead

  • Multi-window mode for watching several streams at once. Tuned keeps to one connection.
  • Lots of knobs. If you like tuning every part of a player, OTT Navigator has more of them.

Where Tuned is ahead

  • Live TV pause that doesn't depend on the provider. Tuned keeps up to an hour of the channel on the device, so pause and rewind work on any live channel, archive or not.
  • Recording and offline downloads.
  • Film and show pages from TMDB, Trakt, and subtitle search.
  • Simple by default. Common choices are already set, and everything else is in Settings.

What Tuned does that most players don't

  • Opens straight to your channels. The playlist and guide live on the device, so the app shows channels the moment it opens and keeps them fresh in the background. Lists page straight from the database, so a playlist with tens of thousands of streams scrolls smoothly.
  • One stream connection, ever. The player, downloads, recordings, channel scans and backup copies take turns on a single connection, and anything in the background waits while you watch. Providers limit connections per account, and Tuned never uses a second one.
  • Live events from your guide. Today's games and fights are pulled out of the guide into one page. Tune finds a working English stream for an event, one channel at a time, and you can follow a team, league or fighter to get an alert before they play.
  • Backup copies and dead channels. When a channel has several copies, Tuned tries the next one if the first won't play, and a channel scan hides channels that never work, without blaming them for a slow internet connection or a busy server.
  • Real names over numbers. Episodes show their real titles from TMDB rather than "S1 E1", and tapping an actor opens everything they've been in, with what's in your playlist marked.
  • Sign in on a TV with your phone. Scan a QR code on the TV and type the login on your phone instead of with the remote.

Which one to pick

If you want a player you can configure endlessly, or several streams at once, OTT Navigator is worth a look. If you want something that opens fast and stays simple while still doing recording, downloads and live pause, try Tuned.
